q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release and forward guidance will likely occur in late August 2026 (approximately 1-2 weeks from today, August 21, 2026). This is extremely soon.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already provided explicit forward guidance for Q2 FY2027: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which translates to a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion.

This is not a forecast—it is the company's own stated guidance released on May 20, 2026. The question asks what the guidance *will be* in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release, which is imminent. Companies typically reaffirm or adjust guidance as they approach quarter-end, but rarely make massive changes at the last moment.

Wall Street consensus sits at $91.9 billion, within NVIDIA's guided range. Q1 FY2027 actual revenue ($81.6 billion) beat the company's guidance, suggesting a pattern of conservative guidance or strong execution.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Major macro shock or customer cancellation occurring in the final 1-2 weeks before earnings
- Unexpected supply chain disruption
- Significant China export restrictions tightening unexpectedly (though guidance already excludes China compute revenue)
- Severe market downturn causing major customer deferrals

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Better-than-expected demand, particularly from cloud customers
- Accelerated AI chip adoption exceeding expectations
- Customer pull-forward demand before potential future restrictions
- Higher ASP (average selling price) on H100/H200 products than baked into guidance
- Following Q1's beat pattern, another strong execution quarter

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The most reliable base rate here is **NVIDIA's own provided guidance**: $91.0 billion ± 2%. The research explicitly states this guidance was released May 20, 2026, for Q2 FY2027. Wall Street consensus is $91.9 billion. Q1 FY2027 actual beat guidance.

---

## Reasoning

Given that:
1. NVIDIA has *already provided* forward guidance of $91.0B ± 2% ($89.2B–$92.8B)
2. The earnings release is imminent (1-2 weeks away)
3. Wall Street consensus ($91.9B) sits comfortably within the guided range
4. NVIDIA has a recent track record of beating its own guidance (Q1 actual > Q1 guidance)
5. There is no indication of a major change in business conditions in the past ~3 months

The most likely outcome is that the forward guidance will fall within the already-published range, likely near the midpoint or slightly above (following the Q1 beat pattern). The probability mass should be concentrated in the $89B–$93B range, with the median near $91–$92B.

The range provided (99.5B–115.5B) is notably *above* the company's own guidance ceiling. This suggests the question may be testing whether I understand that NVIDIA typically doesn't provide wildly aggressive guidance. Values in the 99–115B range would represent a 9–26% sequential increase from Q1 FY2027 ($81.6B), which would be extraordinary even for NVIDIA's growth profile.

I should weight the company's own guidance heavily, as it is the most direct and reliable signal available.

---

High (90th percentile): 93000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, released on May 20, 2026, is an expected **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%** [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-For-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly *does not* assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-For-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range, which has a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion (reported May 20, 2026) was above its own guidance for that quarter [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
